skill.name: mermaid-diagramming
skill.description: Create Mermaid diagrams for Obsidian notes, including flowcharts, sequence diagrams, architecture views, timelines, data charts, and relationship models.
skill.summary: Generate clear Mermaid diagrams and Obsidian-compatible syntax for technical and planning work.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: All 400 cataloged static findings are false positives caused by Mermaid syntax, Markdown fences, labels, and documentation prose. The skill contains no executable scripts, network requests, environment access, filesystem reads, system reconnaissance, or prompt injection evidence. Static review was capped at 400/636 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 236 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

content.value_statement: Complex processes and relationships are difficult to explain in plain text. This skill creates structured Mermaid diagrams that render directly in Obsidian notes.
actual_capabilities: Creates Obsidian-compatible Mermaid blocks for sixteen documented diagram types.
Builds flowcharts, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, and state diagrams from written requirements.
Models schedules, journeys, timelines, database relationships, and Git branching histories.
Produces Sankey, pie, quadrant, and XY charts from structured values.
Applies Mermaid labels, directions, themes, classes, comments, and explicit styles.
Explains syntax choices and common Obsidian rendering constraints.
limitations: Generated diagrams are not rendered or visually verified inside the user's Obsidian installation.
New Mermaid features may fail when Obsidian includes an older Mermaid version.
Obsidian disables JavaScript callbacks and interactive click handlers.
Very large diagrams may render slowly and should be divided into smaller views.

use_cases.title: Document System Workflows
use_cases.description: Turn service interactions, decisions, and dependencies into readable flowcharts or sequence diagrams.

use_cases.title: Plan Projects and Releases
use_cases.description: Visualize milestones, task dependencies, release branches, and roadmap events within project notes.

use_cases.title: Explain Data and Research
use_cases.description: Present relationships, proportions, trends, and conceptual hierarchies as structured diagrams.

prompt_templates.title: Simple Process Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Obsidian-compatible Mermaid flowchart for this process: [steps]. Use clear labels, a top-down direction, and one decision where needed.

prompt_templates.title: Service Interaction Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid sequence diagram for [scenario]. Include these participants: [participants]. Show requests, responses, errors, and activation periods.

prompt_templates.title: Domain Data Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these entities and rules into a Mermaid ER diagram: [entities and relationships]. Include keys, cardinality, and concise relationship labels.

prompt_templates.title: Layered System Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Obsidian-compatible Mermaid architecture diagram for [system]. Group services by layer, label dependencies, identify external systems, and explain compatibility choices.

output_examples.input: A support ticket moves from submission through triage, investigation, resolution, or escalation.
output_examples.output: A top-down flowchart with decision branches for priority, resolution status, and escalation.

output_examples.input: Show a client request passing through an API, authentication service, and database.
output_examples.output: A sequence diagram with participants, synchronous requests, responses, activation periods, and an authentication failure branch.

output_examples.input: Model customers, orders, products, and order items with primary and foreign keys.
output_examples.output: An entity relationship diagram with one-to-many cardinality and clearly labeled keys.

best_practices: Provide the diagram goal, required entities, relationships, and preferred direction.
Keep labels concise and split diagrams that exceed about fifty nodes.
State the Obsidian and Mermaid versions when compatibility is important.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated workflows into one crowded diagram.
Do not request unsupported JavaScript callbacks or click handlers for Obsidian.
Do not omit relationship direction, cardinality, or units when they carry meaning.

faq.question: Which diagram types are supported?
faq.answer: The references cover sixteen types, including flowchart, sequence, class, state, Gantt, ER, architecture, and several data charts.

faq.question: Does the skill work outside Obsidian?
faq.answer: The generated syntax is Mermaid, but the guidance specifically targets Obsidian rendering and version constraints.

faq.question: Can it style diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It can apply explicit colors, classes, themes, labels, comments, and layout directions supported by Mermaid.

faq.question: Can it validate the final rendering?
faq.answer: No. Rendering depends on the Mermaid version, Obsidian theme, installed icon libraries, and local settings.

faq.question: Can it create interactive diagrams?
faq.answer: Obsidian disables JavaScript callbacks and click handlers, so the skill focuses on static diagrams.

faq.question: How should large diagrams be handled?
faq.answer: Divide large models into focused diagrams with shared names and clear links between related views.
